admission.justification: Future reference-only detection changes must retain the declared Markdown content-model boundary: the detector handles clear cases and indented content counts as prose. Extending Markdown parsing must be deliberate; it must not be conflated with executable-code language classification.

alternatives.option: The reference-only detector refuses clear reference-only cases; indented code is prose in this content model.
alternatives.reason: The appendix explicitly bounds the detector to clear cases and classifies indented code as prose, rather than asserting a semantic source parser.

alternatives.option: Treat every apparent reference-only/indented span as executable code that the detector must classify.
alternatives.reason: The appendix explicitly bounds the detector to clear cases and classifies indented code as prose, rather than asserting a semantic source parser.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only if the owning approved requirement is explicitly revised to authorize this changed boundary; this prose is not a computed trigger.

consequences: Preserve the bounded reference-only detector and the existing classification of indented content as prose; do not assert a general executable-code parser.
Rejected unsafe behavior is retained as a boundary, not promoted to a plausible serious alternative; no new implementation, execution or independent acceptance is asserted.
context: MIK-R54 appendix entry 62 retains the chosen current boundary stated in this record. Admission is constrains_future_work, not real_alternatives: the rejected text records disallowed contrary behavior, not evidence that a serious competing design was historically considered. No design-discussion history is inferred from appendix provenance.
